newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-MARSHALL UNFAZED BY RIVAL'S RATING.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-MARSHALL UNFAZED BY RIVAL'S RATING.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Aug 8 - All Black Justin Marshall won't let Springbok rival Joost van der Westhuizen's rating of rugby halfbacks interfere with his game, NZPA reports.
Marshall believes he is part of the world's best team and all that matters to him is his service to the All Blacks rather than individual accolades.
The tigerish South African has been looking for excuses to try and justify his dramatic loss of form recently, Marshall thought.
Van der Westhuizen, once regarded as world rugby's best linkman, has been struggling at the heels of his powerful pack this season.

After the Springboks 32-20 loss to the Wallabies last week, their fourth such result from their last five games, Van der Westhuizen said he wasn't playing as well as he should have been because he was trying too hard for the team's sake.
Then he rated Australian George Gregan as the best halfback in the world at present, with British Lions' Robert Howley next.
He maintained that Marshall was yet to be tested behind a pack on the backfoot.
"As far as I'm concerned it's patch-up stuff, he's got his views," Marshall said.
"If they want to go out and argue with each other every week about who's the best halfback in the world then they can do it.
"As far as I'm concerned I'm in the best team in the world and I'm happy about that. I just want to play well for the side. If accolades come from that, they come; if they don't, they don't.
"I just want to keep playing well, playing well like the team.

"The best thing Joost can do is worry about getting out there and playing the game rather than getting wrapped up in rating of the best halfback in the world. He shouldn't be worrying about that. That's an individual thing that comes from the game."
Marshall thought van der Westhuizen was trying to take on too much responsibility in the Springbok teams.
"He's probably got to ease up a bit.

"He's forcing things a little bit too much and he needs to play himself back into form. I just believe, and it's my personal view, that he should go out and play for the team and get the team on track and everything should fall in place."
Marshall feels he is on top of his game though he hasn't been able to score as many tries as he did last season.
The close attention paid to the former Southland halfback, who moved to Canterbury a few seasons ago, is perhaps the high respect given to his menacing form.
He described his present form as solid.
"I haven't had as many opportunities as I had last year. I think people have sort of become more aware of my game and I've been shut down a little bit I suppose.
"I think my game's been pretty good, my kicking has gone well. My passing, clearance, things like that and the general basis of my game I've been very pleased with.

"When the opportunity comes and there is a chance to take a break, I'll be snatching it -- don't worry about that. It's just a matter of allowing time, there might be just one or two opportunities in a game where I get the chance to run.

"I think people sort of didn't know what to expect for me last year as it was my first year in test rugby. They probably didn't mark me as much as they marked first fives, the Zinnys (Zinzan Brooke) and those guys. The pressure was on them and it created opportunities for me, but this year has been different.
"I don't think it's affected my game at all, I'm just keeping patient. The minute you start forcing things, like Joost is doing at the moment, you start blowing opportunities for the guys out wide.
"We've got such a potent backline that as long as I do my job and do it very well and still be a threat, it's the most important thing.
"To be a threat on the inside you give the opportunities to the people outside.
"If they (opponents) don't watch me then I'll go and if they keep a check on the inside there's going to be opportunities outside. That's what we want as a team.
"So I've just got to keep my work rate right up and work really hard on the field, I'm not taking things for granted.
"I know everybody said what a great test match that was at Ellis Park (won 35-32 by the All Blacks). We thought we had lost. It was just so disappointing when you had to play catch up rugby.
"The emphasis this week has been on the fact that we were lucky to get ourselves out of jail. We've got to take the game to them. We haven't done that this year against South Africa.
"We've trained the way that we're going to go out on the field on Saturday and that's to take the game to them and not take a backward step."
